What to know

  • PCR amplifies a DNA segment. Denaturation, primer annealing, and extension are repeated; the product grows exponentially.
  • Sequencing reads the order of bases. Sanger sequencing uses chain-terminating nucleotides; next-generation sequencing reads millions of fragments in parallel.
  • CRISPR edits DNA at a targeted sequence. A guide RNA directs Cas nuclease to a site; the cell then repairs the break, allowing knockout or correction.
  • Genetic testing has limits. A variant may be pathogenic, benign, or of uncertain significance; interpretation depends on the gene, family history, and evidence.
  • Pharmacogenomics matches drugs to genes. Variants in CYP enzymes, for example, change drug metabolism and can guide dosing.

Check

check.question: What directs Cas9 to a specific DNA sequence?
check.explanation: The guide RNA base-pairs with the target DNA, positioning Cas9 to cut at that site.
